Desktop file I/O, text and JSON serialization

Write student data to a JSON file and read it back as a preview.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A desktop student register

Build a WPF window to add, show, edit and remove students. Compare database storage with exporting data as a JSON text file.

The example can use SQLite or SQL Server. JSON export creates a separate file.

Check the result

Run the Windows desktop app, add a student, select the row and try editing it.

A file is a named box on disk. Serialization turns objects into a format you can save; deserialization turns that saved text back into objects.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Create, read and manipulate files

string folder = Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), "StudyLabData");
Directory.CreateDirectory(folder);
string file = Path.Combine(folder, "notes.txt");
File.WriteAllText(file, "First note");
File.AppendAllText(file, "\nSecond note");
string[] lines = File.ReadAllLines(file);

Path.Combine builds a path using the platform’s separators. Directory.CreateDirectory is safe when the directory already exists. ReadAllText reads one string; ReadAllLines reads an array. Use streams for very large files. Check permission and missing-file errors. Do not build arbitrary file paths from untrusted input.

Serialize student objects

File.WriteAllText(file, JsonSerializer.Serialize(students));
var loaded = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<Student>>(File.ReadAllText(file)) ?? [];

System.Text.Json is included with .NET. The desktop sample exports into students.json under LocalApplicationData/StudyLabData. Expected JSON is an array with id, name and age properties (the exact property case depends on options). Read JSON previews the file; it deliberately does not insert those IDs back into the database. Do not use BinaryFormatter for new code.

Try it yourself

What happens when Read JSON is clicked before Export JSON?

Worked answer

The guarded event handler shows a missing-file message. Export first or add a File.Exists check with a friendly prompt.

Why does re-importing identity IDs need care?

Worked answer

They can conflict with existing rows or database identity rules. Validate the import and define an insert/update policy instead of blindly attaching the objects.

Predict and practise

Does reading a JSON preview automatically insert rows into the database?

Check your prediction

No. Previewing the file and saving database rows are separate actions.

Make one change

Export the student list and open the JSON file as text.

Worked guidance

Find the serialization and file-write calls. Notice property names and values in the output.

Try independently

Export two students and explain how a missing or malformed file should be handled.
